author: Alexey Perevyshin
subject: Isolate beacon components (#90)
body:
* beacon_state: isolate per-group components with append-only deltas and commit-gated reads

Rebuild the beacon state as nine independent per-tier groups (validators,
balances, pending, previous/current participation, inactivity, slot_states,
epoch, longtail), each a finalized base + a Ring of per-fork deltas.

Write model (append-only):
- a writer exists only by rolling (roll_fresh / roll_from /
  roll_fresh_deriving); no by-id re-open API exists anywhere
- an id exists only from Slot::commit(self), which consumes the writer
- StateId (~72 B Copy bundle of nine typed ids, no Default) is assembled
  only by StateWriterView::commit(epoch_idx, longtail_idx); the slots ring
  is deleted — fork-choice nodes own their bundle by value
- StateWriterView is a methodless holder of the 7 per-block tier writers;
  boundary groups (epoch/longtail) travel as separate &mut args and their
  ids — not resolved views — cross any call that may still roll

Read model (one currency):
- StateReadView: pub-field bundle of all nine tier read views, resolved by
  the single BeaconState::read_view(StateId); StateDeltaReadView, hash_view
  and the whole-state delegator surface are deleted
- cross-thread reads are optimistic seqlock (flux's own version counter,
  portable Acquire/Release fences); control starts unwritten so readers
  see None until the first real snapshot publishes
- BeaconState shared via Arc<StateCell>; reader handles cannot dangle
- write() windows exist only for bootstrap and finalization; rolls,
  commits and publish_state_id never block readers

Lifecycle and constructors:
- BeaconState::decompose(ssz, cfg) is the only public constructor;
  empty() deleted; per-tier bases use a single ctor shape
  (capacity + count + SSZ bytes → Result<_, ColumnLenMismatch>)
- owner exposes roll_anchor() instead of raw group accessors
- finalize = reanchor survivors to fresh slots, promote winner into base
  in place, free the tail

Also: merge DeltaBuffer into Ring; hash_tree_root_state takes
&StateReadView; EF/bench harnesses ride { bs: BeaconState, state_id };
fuzz-style concurrency stress tests for the ring with Vec payloads and the
owner/reader protocol; docs/beacon-state-architecture.md describes the
final model (the per-phase migration ledgers are deleted).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Re-applies the branch's per-tier StateReadView migration to the storage

nothing can be validated) and adds main's decompressed_pubkeys param to

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* checkpoint persist re-homed onto the groups (origin/main PRs #79/#83)

Encoding: each finalized base owns its SSZ body (write_ssz /
write_ssz_range / per-queue writers); encode.rs mirrors decompose.rs as
the cross-group dispatcher (fixed part + section order + offsets), with
Section kept crate-private. Immutable regains the raw historical_roots
(frozen post-Capella) — a hash can't be re-encoded.

Consistency: BeaconStateReader::begin_checkpoint() -> CheckpointCursor
(plain position + version token) and checkpoint_chunk(&mut cursor, &mut
buf) pull the state out part by part. Sync is internal: every chunk is
version-checked before and after encoding (torn bytes are re-encoded,
never returned); a superseding finalize is waited out and surfaces as
Restarted with the cursor back at part 0 on the NEWER state — the
storage tile only truncates its temp files and keeps stepping.

Realloc safety for the unversioned base reads:
- pending + longtail groups get a promote barrier (internal mutex taken
  by finalize's base promote and the section writers); STF-path reads
  stay lock-free references
- slot eth1_votes: allocation pinned at MAX_ETH1_VOTES + a manual
  SlotState::clone_from (the derived impl replaced the Vec allocation,
  silently breaking promote's stability contract)
- validators pubkey index behind RwLock (from main's automerge)

decompose grows the optional pre-decompressed pubkey sidecar param
(single ctor; verified against canonical compressed keys); the tile's
bootstrap decodes the sidecar with a decompress fallback. Storage's
CheckpointWriter shrinks to file lifecycle (temp paths, buffering,
truncate-on-restart, atomic rename-commit; slot re-read at commit since
a restart may advance it). e2e gates and benches ride the cursor; new
in-crate encode->decompose fixed-point + sidecar round-trip tests;
mainnet fixture round-trips byte-exact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* beacon tile: port the data-availability gating (origin/main PRs #82/#84/#87/#88)

Feedback::AwaitData(B256) (+ hex Debug): a fully-prechecked blob block
is withheld from the STF until the storage tile signals
DataColumnsAvailable; held blocks live in dc_pending_blocks, available
roots in dc_available, both pruned at finalization. apply_block_impl
takes gate_da (false for try_apply_block); the boundary is
max(sync_finalized_slot from PM targets, finalized slot). Orphan
buffering now always holds the block and requests the parent only when
following and not already held for DA. Checkpoint anchor epoch uses
div_ceil (PR #85).

Also fixes a replay bug the port surfaced: handle_rpc only matched
BlocksRangeResp while pending-block replays injected BlocksRootResp,
silently dropping every replayed RPC block — collapsed to
handle_rpc_block with no message discrimination (main's shape).

All three sync scenarios pass (blob block held → released on
DataColumnsAvailable → state root matches the EF post-state).

author: Bronek Kozicki
subject: Add CONTEXT.md, the project glossary for humans and coding agents (#180)
body:
The file follows the domain-modeling convention from Matt Pocock's
skills collection for AI coding agents (github.com/mattpocock/skills).
Its principles, briefly:

- One canonical term per concept, chosen deliberately; the synonyms a
  reader might reach for are listed under "Avoid". Vocabulary drift --
  "service" here, "worker" there, for the same thing -- is how naming
  fragments over time, and coding agents drift faster than humans do.
- A definition says what a thing IS, in one or two sentences. The file
  is a glossary only: no implementation details, no spec, no scratch
  pad. Those live in docs/ and in the code.
- It grows lazily. A term is added when it crystallises in design or
  review, never speculatively; an entry that has to be argued about is
  an entry that was added too early.
- It serves agents as much as people: agent tooling built on these
  skills reads the glossary before exploring the codebase and sticks to
  its vocabulary in everything it produces -- code, issue text, review
  comments -- so generated output speaks the project's language instead
  of inventing its own.

Silver benefits more than most: tile, spine, and TCache read as generic
English but name precise architectural commitments here, and the
glossary is where that precision is pinned.

The sibling convention, decision records under docs/adr/, records
choices that are hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the
result of a real trade-off. The first ADRs arrive with the Beacon API
work (#81), where both conventions are already in day-to-day use.

subject: Per-tile attestation-root memo + honest Immutable + microbenchmarks (#181)
body:
* Memoize gossip attestation roots in a per-tile AttestationRootMemo

Post-Electra all single attestations of a slot share 1-3 distinct
128-byte AttestationData values, yet hash_attestation_data +
compute_signing_root ran once per message. The memo is a plain field on
BeaconStateTile (the tile owns its thread: no locks, no TLS), keyed on
the full AttestationData bytes, capped at 64 entries with slot-floor
pruning in slot_tick (the AttestationPool idiom). Each cached signing
root is paired with the exact domain it was derived under and served
only on byte-equal match, so a fork transition can never yield a stale
root. verify_single_attestation takes the caller-derived roots; the
aggregate path reuses the memo for its coverage key and threads the
data root into hash_tree_root_aggregate_and_proof, removing that path's
duplicate inner-attestation hash (fulu + gloas variants, equivalence
pinned by an ssz-level test). Hit/Miss/Full shmem counters expose the
hit rate.

Criterion bench (crates/beacon_state/tile/benches/attestation_root_memo),
50k messages, one thread: D=2 19.96 ms unmemoized vs 0.47 ms memoized
(~42x); D=5000 adversarial spray past the cap costs +0.75% over
unmemoized - the bounded worst case. Not visible in `just perf-local`:
the harness replays range-sync blocks and produces no attestation
gossip.

Adversarially reviewed (correctness, stale-value/poisoning attacks, ssz
semantic drift vs HEAD, EMFILE/memory bounds, #174 relay interaction):
no blockers; the +0.75% spray cost and pre-validation aggregate-path
Miss inflation are accepted and documented.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

* Evict the fork-data-root cache from Immutable

Immutable carried the one thing about it that was not immutable: a
5-entry fork-data-root table refreshed via refresh_fork_data_roots(&mut
self) at state load, with pub fork-version/gvr fields that silently
invalidated the private cache unless callers remembered the refresh.
The choreography existed only to keep version-keyed entries fresh - a
problem the keying already solves.

The table moves next to AttestationRootMemo as ForkDataRoots, a lazy
(version -> root) table on the tile: keyed by version, an entry can
never go stale; a stored genesis_validators_root guards re-anchoring.
Only handle_attestation (up to ~50k messages/slot) uses it. Every other
former caller - the aggregate/exit/bls-change/proposer-slashing gossip
paths and all STF sites - now derives the domain directly via
bls::compute_domain: one sha256 compression (~55 ns measured), at most
a few times per block, under 100 us/slot in total against the 170 ms
apply p50. Immutable is left honestly immutable.

Adversarially reviewed: all 18 rewritten sites audited for
(domain_type, version, gvr) transposition - none found; EF operation /
sanity / transition / fork-choice vectors pass; the nonzero-gvr
handle_attestation test added on review feedback is the only pin on the
gvr wiring (all other signing tests run with gvr = 0).

author: Owen
subject: adds beacon api (#81)
body:
* adds beacon api

* Documentation of planned Beacon API work

* Extract HTTP server byte machine into silver_httpcore

First step of the client_server tile consolidation (docs/adr/0001): the
HTTP/1.1 connection state machine (parse, keep-alive, pipelining, response
framing) moves out of beacon_api into a new transport-free crate with
bytes-only interfaces, so it can be tested without sockets and shared with
the client role next. beacon_api keeps its tile, poll, and endpoints
unchanged; behavior is byte-identical. Framing tests move with the machine
and gain deterministic chunking coverage (single-byte feeds, pipelined
requests split across feeds, oversize rejection, dispatch-after-drain).

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

* Move HTTP client machine into silver_httpcore; delete dead IPC transport

Second step of the client_server consolidation (docs/adr/0001, 0002): the
engine's connection byte machine (request framing, Content-Length response
parsing, partial-I/O resumption) moves to silver_httpcore as the client-role
sibling of the server machine, and the transport becomes the closed-set
Stream enum (Tcp | Uds). The newline-framed ipc.rs (dead code) is deleted;
Unix-socket support is now the same HTTP pool over Stream::Uds, proven by a
real UDS round-trip test asserting the JWT bearer header on the wire.

Engine keeps all protocol: pool policy, JSON-RPC, JWT, correlation, ReqKind
dispatch. The newPayload transcode path is untouched (verified: one body
copy before and after). Request framing is pinned by golden-byte tests
captured from the previous implementation.

New: EngineConfig::max_connections (default 32) bounds the previously
unbounded pool; spine intake gates on pool capacity via consume_one, so
excess requests wait on the queue. Healthcheck issuance gates on capacity
too. A connect that cannot start (resolve/connect/register error) now fails
the rpc through the normal error path instead of stranding it forever --
previously masked by unbounded pool growth, fatal under a cap.

Behavior notes: an empty Content-Length value is now rejected instead of
read as zero; the Connecting-state error checks for UDS follow the TCP
shape (the old distrusting variant was unreachable dead code).

Known limitation (follow-up tracked in Linear): no per-request deadline, so
an EL that accepts requests but never responds can gate intake while the
engine_reqs ring (1024 slots) overwrites oldest entries.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5

* Table-based dispatch for beacon_api routes

Third step of the client_server consolidation (docs/adr/0003): the inline
exact-match path closure becomes a const route table -- (method, pattern,
handler fn) compiled once at init into literal/param segments, linearly
scanned, with zero-alloc borrowed params (inline capacity 4). The router

* Linger on a refused request instead of resetting it

A request refused from its headers — a body declared past the read cap, or
framing that was never established — is answered while the peer may still
be sending. Closing then leaves those bytes unread, and the peer sees a
reset where the answer should be.

The two outcomes are not equivalent to the client. go-eth2-client turns a
delivered 413 into an *api.Error, which its multi-client wrapper spares as
a 4xx (multi/client.go:186); a connection that dies before a parseable
response is a transport error that fails errors.As, falls through to the
default failover (multi/client.go:200) and deactivates the node, with
recovery gated on two unsynchronised 30 s tickers. Which one a deployment
sees is decided by socket buffering and by how net/http interleaves its
write and read loops — nothing the client can settle. Answering the same
way every time is the server's job.

So the connection now half-closes after the answer drains and keeps
reading: the peer sees its response, marked Connection: close, terminated
by FIN, and the body still in flight is read and discarded rather than
left to reset the connection carrying it. The drain ends on the peer's own
close, and is bounded by nginx's lingering_close caps — 5 s between reads,
30 s in total — so a slot cannot be held by a client that keeps sending or
by one that neither sends nor hangs up. Unix sockets take the same
half-close: an unread body breaks the peer's send there too.

Limits: the drain costs a refused connection up to 5 s of a slot where it
previously closed at once, and the discarded bytes are read at whatever
rate the peer sends them — the per-event drain is bounded by scheduling,
not structurally.

* Derive the network's name from its genesis fork version

SpecConfig carried two independent notions of network identity:
CONFIG_NAME, defaulting to "mainnet" whenever a config file left it out,
and network_name(), which read the same identity off genesis_fork_version.
A sepolia config without CONFIG_NAME served "mainnet" from
GET /eth/v1/config/spec while its fork versions said otherwise, every
devnet served "mainnet" outright, and a file setting one and not the
other split them silently. No validator client cross-checks the two, but
they use them independently — Teku's --network auto preloads a builtin
base config by CONFIG_NAME while signing domains come from the fork
versions — so a body contradicting itself hands a client two different
networks.

CONFIG_NAME is now optional and network_name() is the one identity: the
configured name when a file gives one, the name genesis_fork_version
carries otherwise, and an empty name reads as absent. An unrecognised
fork version yields devnet-<hex>, unprefixed, because go-eth2-client
decodes every 0x-prefixed spec value into a byte slice and would hand its
consumers bytes where they read a string. Loading a file whose
CONFIG_NAME contradicts a fork version silver knows by name warns and
continues — only the operator knows which half is the typo — and the
comparison is exact: Teku's builtin lookup is, and upstream names are
lowercase.

Devnet telemetry vocabulary changes with it: meta_network_name goes from
0x<hex> to devnet-<hex>, so an already-running devnet deployment splits
its identity at the deploy boundary.

* Share one readiness loop between the tile's two HTTP tenants

The beacon-api server and the engine-api client each owned an mio `Poll`,
so every `loop_body` of the application-boundary tile made two
`epoll_wait` calls to learn about sockets on one thread. Both now register
through one `Readiness`, and a single wait feeds both dispatches.

Sharing a loop shares a token space, and a token both tenants could
allocate would deliver one tenant's socket readiness into the other's
dispatch — where an API client hanging up fails the engine call that
happens to share its number. `TokenRange` partitions the space instead:
each tenant takes `share(index, TENANTS)`, allocates only inside its own
range, and skips events whose token falls outside it. Both halves are
enforced rather than documented: `at` asserts the offset is inside the
span, and each tenant asserts at construction that its range holds every
socket it can register at once — listeners plus the connection cap for the
server, the pool cap plus the first-run healthcheck's overshoot for the
client.

The server's connection offsets recycle over its range above the
listeners. Connections close in any order while the cursor only advances,
so the offset it wraps onto may still be held; the allocator probes
forward past live offsets, and the construction assert is what guarantees
it lands on a free one rather than replacing a live connection's map
entry.

Because a tenant now sees only the batch the shared wait produced, the
order inside `loop_body` decides latency: taking a request off the spine
flips its pooled connection's interest to WRITABLE, so the wait runs after
that intake and the request goes on the wire in the iteration that took
it. Measured on the tile's own tests, produce-to-wire is 1 iteration per
request where waiting first cost 2, and 1000 iterations make exactly 1000
`epoll_wait` calls against one epoll instance, down from 2000 against two.

The engine's dispatch walks that batch once, indexing connections by
token offset, instead of scanning every event once per connection — the
batch carries the server's events too, so the old shape cost
O(connections x events) over both tenants' sockets.

Limits: the timeout stays zero, so the loop still busy-polls; a blocking
wait needs an `mio::Waker` on the flux work signal, which is separate. The
healthcheck is enqueued inside the engine's spin, after the wait, so it
alone still reaches the EL an iteration late. And `share` truncates:
`usize::MAX / count` leaves the tokens above the last share owned by
nobody, which costs nothing while nothing allocates there.

ADR 0004's amendment described this loop as outstanding work; it now
describes the loop, leaving the waker and the timeout as what remains.

* Answer 431 when a head outgrows the read buffer

A request head that filled the whole 16 MiB read buffer without ever
completing was dropped where it stood: read_space reported exhaustion,
dispatch had no complete request to answer, and the connection died by
reset with nothing on the wire. That contradicted the read loop's own
rule — a full buffer always leaves something to answer with — and a
reset before a parseable response is the failure mode validator-client
stacks punish hardest.

cap is a 413 from its headers, garbage is a 400. The unfinished head now
gets the 431 of RFC 6585, framed and lingered like every other reject,
so the sender reads the status instead of a reset.

The equivalent fix landed in flux's HTTP machine during its adversarial
review rounds; this carries it to the silver machine the flux one will
eventually replace.

author: vladimir-ea
subject: gossipsub 13 (#260)
body:
* network: emit tiny inbound gossip frames

A frame completing inside the varint read-ahead committed its
reservation without emitting NetEvent::Gossip, so frames up to nine
bytes vanished before the handler. A gossipsub 1.3 extensions-only
RPC is six bytes and takes exactly this path. The length state now
parses buffered excess before reading, so a complete buffered frame
also survives a FIN arriving right behind it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* network: negotiate meshsub 1.3 with 1.2 fallback

Meshsub 1.3 is always negotiated: proposed on outbound gossip
streams, accepted inbound, advertised via identify, with 1.2 as the
multistream fallback. Streams keep their negotiated version, with
classification via is_gossip, so the gossip handler can scope
extension announcements per stream. On a negotiated 1.3 stream the
extensions announcement is the first RPC, restarting on stream
recreation via the write state; it stays empty until an extension
is enabled. Outbound na detection compared header+na at the
post-header offset, so version fallback never fired for any
protocol; a reject is the once-only header then a bare na, matching
our own responder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gossip: plumb partial modes and peer capabilities

PartialColumnsMode (default Off) is validated at startup: non-Off
modes are unsupported and rejected. Data-column subscriptions emit
capability flags with the registry implication applied
(requestsPartial implies sending support). Extension announcements
are stream-scoped: only the first RPC of a meshsub 1.3 stream
counts, and any replacement stream resets the peer's capability, so
an announcement-less or 1.2 stream turns it off. Per-peer subnet
masks replace on each update and clear on unsubscribe. Nothing sets
our own partial flags while the mode is Off.

author: vladimir-ea
subject: gossip fork domains (#264)
body:
* gossip: route messages with explicit fork domains

Replaces the GossipHandler's single fork_digest_hex with ActiveDomains,
which holds the current domain plus at most one neighbour (the next
domain during advance subscription, or the previous while it drains).
Inbound topics parse against the routable domains; unknown digests are
ignored, never penalised. NewGossipMsg and PeerEvent::SendGossip carry
the originating GossipDomain, so a message is forwarded and IHAVE'd
only on the domain it arrived on, never rewrapped. The message cache
keys IHAVE tracking by (topic, domain). The control tile derives the
current domain from the status fork digest and the wall-slot-scheduled
fork. GossipDomain lives in silver_common; ForkName gains Hash.

The transition schedule (advance subscription, wall-clock cutover,
drain) and the peer-manager (digest, topic) rekeying are follow-ups;
ActiveDomains already accepts the second domain they will drive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* peer: carry the fork digest on gossip control messages

The subscribe/unsubscribe/graft/prune PeerControls now carry the
digest of the domain they target, and the gossip handler wires each
onto that digest's topic string rather than the single current
domain. The peer manager supplies its current digest at every emit
site. Behaviour is unchanged with one active domain; this is the
plumbing the two-mesh overlap builds on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* peer: split gossip meshes by fork domain

Each topic's mesh becomes mesh::TopicMeshes, a Single/Multi enum that
carries one digest normally and two across a fork overlap, each with
independent membership. Graft/prune/leave and forward routing act on
a specific digest; membership queries, gauges and dead-entry sweeps
stay semantic across all live digests. Scoring and backoff remain
keyed by the semantic GossipTopic: a maintenance prune still backs a
peer off on both digests, while the administrative cutover drain
prunes without backoff. set_active_domains diffs each topic's meshes
and drives the Single<->Multi transitions, subscribing a newly-active
digest and unsubscribing a drained one. The inbound graft/prune/
subscribe events carry the parsed digest so membership lands on the
right sub-mesh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* common: encapsulate GossipDomain behind a constructor and accessors

GossipDomain's fields are now private, constructed via
GossipDomain::new and read via digest()/format() (all const). Keeps
the digest/format representation an implementation detail of the
type rather than open at every call site.

subject: Make the G2 decompression kernel translatable by Aeneas (#383)
body:
Charon and Aeneas can now translate decompress_g2::decompress and every
function it calls into Lean. Aeneas cannot translate iterator adaptors, so
those loops become index loops:

- iter_mut().enumerate() and iter().enumerate() loops index directly.
- Loops over (0..n).rev() count down with while loops.
- Z_BITS.contains(&bit) becomes five comparisons.
- reduce_row calls muladd_row, since IFMA products commute.
- The blst_p2_affine for each lane is built in a helper, point. Aeneas
  silently dropped the last field write when the struct was built inside
  the loop body.

The new #[inline] hints change LLVM's inlining: scott_membership is now
inlined into decompress, and times_minus_z stays out of line. Without
them, the loop changes alone measured about 0.25% slower. A crate-level
allow covers clippy's needless_range_loop, with the reason.

g2_parse in crates/beacon_state/tile/benches/bls_verify.rs, isolated core
12 of a Ryzen 9 9950X, four interleaved runs per binary, mean of means:

  row          main        this change
  simd/8       98.26 us    98.10 us   (-0.16%)
  simd/16      196.56 us   196.06 us  (-0.25%)
  simd/1024    12.579 ms   12.545 ms  (-0.27%)
  blst rows    within -0.15% to +0.12%

Part of the gain is likely code layout, which unrelated changes can move.

author: Adrian Chifor
subject: Tighten input validation in p2p decoding paths (#446)
body:
* Bound discv5 authdata-size to the largest valid header

Packet::decode checked authdata-size only against the packet length.
The auth data is copied into fixed 512-byte buffers, so not every such
value fits.

The largest valid auth data is a handshake carrying a maximal ENR.
Reject anything above that.

* Harden libp2p public key decoding

Length-delimited protobuf fields were bounds-checked with an unchecked
`pos + len`. Use checked_add and get, so out-of-range lengths return an
error.

The TLS verifier derived the PeerId from the raw protobuf encoding of the
host key. Accept only a 33-byte compressed secp256k1 key, as libp2p clients
send. Derive the PeerId from the key itself, so one key maps to one PeerId.

* Bound the identify body copy by its declared length

Bytes read together with the length prefix were copied into the body
without checking that they fit. Return an error when they exceed the
declared length.

Also fail a 10-byte length prefix with no terminating byte, instead of
waiting on an empty read buffer.

* Avoid Instant overflow when advertising a prune backoff

The advertised backoff was rounded up through f64, which loses precision
for very large deadlines. Round up with integer arithmetic, and skip
recording an advertisement that Instant cannot represent.

* Validate the Gloas bid commitments offset in check_canonical

check_canonical size-checked the signed bid but not the inner
ExecutionPayloadBid offset, which blob_kzg_commitments slices from.

Run ExecutionPayloadBidView::check_size on the bid message as well.

* Clamp empty-slot marking to the sync window

block_received iterated every slot between the parent and the block.
update already ignores slots outside the window, so iterate only that
range. The loop is now bounded for any slot value.

* Handle empty snappy frames in the decoder

A frame with a zero-length payload left `need` equal to the header length.
The decoder then treated the complete frame as a pending header and made
no progress.

Process an empty frame as soon as its header completes. Padding and
skippable frames are skipped; other types fail as before.

author: Adrian Chifor
subject: Bound per-connection QUIC and req/resp resources (#447)
body:
* Cap QUIC connection receive window and disable unused stream types

quinn's default connection receive window is unbounded. Set it to 16 MiB,
close to rust-libp2p's 15 MB. It must stay above the bandwidth-delay
product, since throughput caps at window / RTT.

libp2p uses neither unidirectional streams nor QUIC datagrams. Grant zero
uni streams and no datagram buffer, as rust-libp2p does.

* Close a superseded inbound gossip stream

A newly negotiated inbound gossip stream replaced the tracked one but left
it open, together with any in-progress tcache reservation.

Remove the old stream, as rust-libp2p and go-libp2p-pubsub do. Dropping its
read state aborts the reservation.

gossip_stall_closes_connection opened two gossip streams by accident. It now
reuses the stream it opened.

* Bound DataColumnSidecarsByRoot requests at the spec maximum

The by-root request bound was MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE (10 MiB).
The Fulu request type is List[DataColumnsByRootIdentifier,
MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB]. Each element costs a 4-byte offset plus at
most DC_BY_ROOT_ID_MAX bytes. That gives 136,192 bytes, matching
Lighthouse's limit.

DataColumnsByRootRequestView::check_size accepts at most this size, so no
request the storage decoder accepts is rejected.

* Reject RPC error responses longer than ErrorMessage

ErrorMessage is List[byte, 256]. A larger declared length was read into a
256-byte buffer and then waited for the response timeout.

Reject it before reading the body.

* Bound framed snappy bytes per RPC chunk

The decoder skipped padding and skippable frames without limit.

The consensus spec bounds the encoding of n bytes by
max_compressed_len(n) = 32 + n + n // 6. Each chunk may now consume that
plus the stream identifier and one header and CRC per 64 KiB frame.
Lighthouse applies max_compress_len(n) to the whole framed stream, so
interoperating encoders fit this looser bound.

The check is one add and one compare per frame header.

author: Adrian Chifor
subject: Validate addresses before admitting inbound QUIC connections under load (#448)
body:
* Require address validation for the trusted-IP cap bypass

Connections from trusted IPs skip the connection cap. Over the cap, a
trusted source now passes a stateless Retry first, so only a validated
address uses the bypass.

The overflow stops at twice the cap, the size of the peer manager's slot
table.

* Retry unvalidated Initials under handshake pressure

The connection cap counted half-open handshakes like established peers.

Inbound handshakes in flight are now counted until they complete or close.
Beyond 16 in flight, or within 16 slots of the cap, an unvalidated Initial
gets a Retry first. Peers pay one extra round trip, and only in those
states.

* Cap inbound QUIC connections per source IP

Nothing bounded inbound connections per address before the handshake. The
peer manager scores IP colocation only afterwards.

Admit at most 8 inbound connections per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64. That
leaves room for several nodes behind one NAT. Trusted IPs and loopback are
exempt. An unvalidated repeat source gets a Retry first.

* Log rejected QUIC Initials at debug level

Endpoint::accept failures for malformed Initials logged at error level and
fed the per-callsite error counters. Keep the log, at debug level.

author: Adrian Chifor
subject: discv5: match responses to requests, tighten IP voting and table admission (#449)
body:
* Accept WHOAREYOU only for a recent request nonce

Per the wire spec, a WHOAREYOU must echo the nonce of a packet we sent. We
matched it to a peer by source address, and skipped the nonce check on a
live session.

Record the nonces of our probes, PINGs and FINDNODEs for one request
timeout. Accept a WHOAREYOU only for a recorded nonce, from the address we
sent to. A mismatched WHOAREYOU no longer consumes the pending probe nonce.

* Require a live majority before IP votes move our ENR

Votes never expired, and an address needed only ip_vote_threshold (3)
votes to update our ENR and the libp2p identify address.

Votes now live in an IpVotes owner type and expire after 30 minutes, as in
sigp/discv5. Peers refresh theirs on every PONG. The winning address must
reach the threshold and hold a strict majority of live votes in its address
family. A peer's vote is dropped when it is evicted or banned.

The default threshold stays at 3, so small testnets still learn their
address.

* Bound the fork digest tally

seen_fork_digests gained a key for every digest seen in NODES replies and
was never pruned. log_table_state formats and sorts it every 12 seconds.

Ignore new digests once 64 are tracked. Known digests still count.

* Record session nonces only after decryption succeeds

The replay nonce was stored and last_active refreshed before the message
was authenticated.

The replay check now only reads the ring. The nonce is recorded and the
session refreshed once AES-GCM decryption succeeds.

* Reject handshake ENRs with trailing bytes

Enr::decode stops at the end of the RLP list and ignores what follows. A
handshake record with trailing bytes was stored raw and later served in our
NODES replies.

Decode handshake records with alloy_rlp::decode_exact. NODES records need no
change, since message decoding slices each one to its RLP length.

* Reject out-of-range PONG ports and non-v4 handshake sizes

The PONG port was decoded as u64 and truncated to u16. Decode it as u16.

Handshake decoding read the signature and ephemeral key at fixed offsets
and ignored the sig-size and eph-key-size bytes. The v4 identity scheme is
the only one we support, so sizes other than 64 and 33 are rejected.

* Key handshake challenges by node id and address

Challenges were keyed by node id alone, so packets for the same id from
different addresses shared one entry.

Key them by (node id, socket address), as sigp/discv5 does. A challenge is
still removed before the signature check, also as in sigp/discv5.

The per-IP WHOAREYOU limit now groups IPv6 sources by /64.

* Admit handshake peers to the table only at their advertised address

Any identity that completed a handshake was inserted into the routing
table, evicting the bucket's LRU even when it had a live session.

A new peer now enters the table only when its ENR's UDP endpoint equals the
packet source, as in sigp/discv5. It goes through the normal insert, so a
full bucket parks it as pending.

The session is kept either way. Messages from session peers outside the
table are now answered instead of dropped, so nodes behind NAT still get
PONGs and NODES. NodeFound is still emitted from the handshake ENR.

insert_or_update_evicting has no caller left and is removed.

* Accept NODES only as answers to our own FINDNODE

NODES packets were processed whatever their request id, total or
distances.

Track outstanding FINDNODEs by request id in FindNodeRequests, with the
target node and the requested distances. Drop a NODES packet that answers
none of them, and any node not at a requested log2 distance. A request
accepts at most 16 packets and expires after 5 seconds. A record with a
lower seq than the stored one is ignored.

The PING-driven ENR refresh waits while a FINDNODE to that peer is in
flight.

* Keep request nonces for longer than request_timeout

Request nonces expired with request_timeout (500 ms by default), checked at
each cleanup. A WHOAREYOU from a peer with a longer round trip could then
miss its nonce, and that handshake failed until the next attempt.

Keep them for 2 seconds instead. request_timeout still governs PONGs.

author: Adrian Chifor
subject: gossipsub: seed message-id hashing and bound IWANT serving (#450)
body:
* Seed message-id and fast-dedup hashing

Maps keyed by MessageId hashed only the first 8 id bytes. IHAVE and
IDONTWANT ids come from peers, so those bytes are not guaranteed to be
uniformly distributed.

The fast dedup hash was an unkeyed FxHash, and a hit counts as a duplicate
without comparing content.

Both now use foldhash with a random seed. MessageId hashes as two
fixed-width writes, keeping lookups near the old cost. Payload hashing gets
about 5x faster on 2 KiB and 128 KiB bodies.

* Bound IWANT serving per peer per heartbeat

The per-id retransmission limit lives in a direct-mapped filter shared with
IDONTWANT, so an evicted slot loses its serve count.

Serve at most max_ihave_length IWANT ids per peer per heartbeat, the most a
compliant peer asks for. Record at most 1000 IDONTWANT ids per peer per
heartbeat. Normal traffic stays far below both limits.

* Require canonical subnet ids in gossip topics

str::parse accepted non-canonical spellings, such as a leading zero or a
plus sign. Message ids hash the raw topic string, so those spellings got
distinct ids.

Accept only decimal digits with no leading zero, except "0" itself.

* Dedup and penalise corrupt snappy gossip bodies

A body that failed decompression got no dedup entry or penalty, unlike a
body with a bad length.

Mirror the bad-length path: record the invalid-snappy id in dedup and emit
P2pGossipInvalidMsg once. Repeats now stop at the fast duplicate check.
